standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the reduction to the reduced case at the start of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Integral closure of a one-dimensional Noetherian domain is semi-local Dedekind
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the rings A_j used in the construction.

core_obligations: Use the power-works lemma to replace A by A modulo the intersection of the minimal primes, so that A may be assumed reduced (proof lines 7639-7641).

Replace K by the image of K -> L, so that K is reduced and Spec(L) -> Spec(K) is surjective and closed, hence Spec(K) is a finite discrete space and K is a finite product of fields (proof lines 7642-7645).

List the minimal primes p_j of A and let A_j be the normalization of A/p_j, a semi-local Dedekind domain with at least one maximal ideal, and let n be the sum of the numbers of maximal ideals of the A_j (proof lines 7648-7655).
Complete the construction of a in the maximal ideal and x in K with equal images in L and with m_A equal to the radical of (a), which occupies the remainder of the proof up to line 7708.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to A reduced and K a finite product of fields.
Introduce the normalizations of the quotients by the minimal primes.
Construct the matching elements using a count of maximal ideals.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring A with product of minimal-prime localizations L and an integral ring map K -> L, there are a in the maximal ideal and x in K with the same image in L and with the maximal ideal equal to the radical of (a). The proof reduces A via the power-works lemma to the reduced case, replaces K by its image so that K is reduced and Spec(K) is a finite discrete space, hence K is a finite product of fields (proof lines 7639-7645). It then lists the minimal primes of A, sets A_j to be the normalization of A/p_j (a semi-local Dedekind domain), and proceeds to construct the required element by summing the numbers of maximal ideals and choosing a and x accordingly (proof lines 7648 onwards). H2: the reduction to a finite product of fields and the subsequent construction through the normalizations are the substance; the author marks two auxiliary steps as 'some details omitted', which concern only the reduction and the closedness of Spec(L) -> Spec(K).
